Brigitte Eggerstedt Adam Deixel In the 18th and 19th centuries, particularly in German-speaking regions, the term “Religionsweiser” referred to a Jewish religious teacher or preacher. This title was used when a Jewish community did not have an official rabbi. The "Religionsweiser" assumed the most important rabbinical and religious duties in daily life like

Dear Ones,
I arrived safely in Paris without any major hitches. In London, I wasn't able to meet up with my cousin—well, as they say, c'est la vie. In Paris, a French customs officer eyed my passport suspiciously but eventually decided to let me through. I suppose the French aren't very fond of communist passports. After I cleared passport control, people from the American group approached me and asked who I was and what the problem had been. Those are such stereotypical questions. In the end, it all ended with a smile. Alina and Claude were waiting for me. And what comes next? Well, on November 21st, I’m flying to Poland. Once again, I would like to thank you both—my dear uncle and aunt—with my deepest gratitude for looking after me. You cared for me as if I were your own child, and I thank you so very much for that. I will always remember it. I would also really like to take this opportunity to once again dispel Auntie’s doubts regarding her cooking. Dearest Auntie, I truly enjoy your cooking—what you make, and how you make it. Just ask Tosia if I ever complained!

Bogdan
